title: Macroeconomics and Business Cycles
text: Macroeconomics is the branch of economics dealing with the structure, performance, behavior, and decision-making of an economy as a whole. Key macroeconomic variables include GDP, unemployment, inflation, and the balance of trade. Business cycles are recurring fluctuations in economic activity, consisting of expansions (periods of growth) and recessions (periods of decline). The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) officially dates U.S. recessions. Major macroeconomic theories include Keynesian, monetarist, and real business cycle models. Macroeconomic policy is conducted through fiscal policy (government spending and taxation) and monetary policy (central bank interest rates and money supply).
